Peter MacKay: Respect the rule of law

MaCay's argument rests on the idea of a democratic parliament functioning in a democratic manner, it's an argument I have taken issue with many times in the past because I believe that it is neither.

If we look at our 'democratically elected parliament ' we find a group of MP's from different parties, each of whom [in the majority of cases] was elected by the greatest minority of their constituents. In the last election the Liberals came out ahead in this race by willing 39.5% of the popular vote which allowed them to take 54% of the seats, it's electoral math like that that gives them pretty well carte blanche for the next four years - is rule by the greatest minority democracy?

If we look further into how our parliamentary democracy works we see that these MP's do not control their own votes. On important pieces of legislation they are told how they will vote by their party leader and, with few exceptions, they follow their orders because their first duty is to the party leader and not the greatest minority of people who elected them. If our representatives are not free is that democracy?

And even if we did take MacKay's premise that our MP's were elected democratically, and operate in a democratic parliament as truth, those individuals are still constrained by the living document that is the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms - lest we find our selves subject to the will of the greatest minority.... told how and when to vote by their party leader.

MacKay and his ilk hope you don't think to much about things like that as they attempt to tug at your heart strings by invoking "society’s most vulnerable", don't be fooled, this is about lifting Constitutional constraints on less than democratic institutions and nothing more. If they're reduced to plucking at our heart strings they already know they don't have an argument that will stand on its own - emotion is all they've got, and emotions are a very poor basis for fair laws.
